endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Determine if key stakeholders have been identified and whether tracking of key stakeholder involvement has been established.

endorsements.title: Key decision points in adopting an AI solution
endorsements.issuer: Health AI Partnership (Duke Health and partners)
endorsements.quote: This decision point features guides for identifying and prioritizing problems within health care delivery organizations and surfacing stakeholders affected by problems.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Measure the rate at which recommendations from security checks and incidents are implemented.

endorsements.title: A strategic pathway for the ethical development of AI tools in dementia care
endorsements.issuer: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
endorsements.quote: Involve a diverse range of stakeholders, including people with ADRD, caregivers, healthcare providers, ethicists, business professionals, and technical developers, in the integration of AI systems from the early stages.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied tests whether identifying affected stakeholder groups and tracking their involvement reduces unassessed risks from AI tools, and no study documents the hazard itself. Support for the practice rests on five endorsing sources, four of them frameworks or guidance and one a commentary.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero documenting the hazard. The five endorsements reflect expert consensus rather than measured effects. The NIST AI 600-1 excerpt addresses the rate at which security recommendations are implemented, which bears only indirectly on stakeholder tracking. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

The dementia care commentary calls for involving people with ADRD, caregivers, clinicians, ethicists, and developers from the early stages. No supplied study measures whether such involvement changes patient safety, trust, or access to a human, so the benefit to patients remains an expectation rather than a finding.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare AI deployments with and without a documented stakeholder identification and tracking process, measuring whether risks to specific groups are detected before go-live and whether post-deployment harms differ. Such studies should also record the staff time and cost of maintaining involvement logs.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems cannot yet tell from the evidence whether stakeholder tracking surfaces the risks these groups face, although the practice's stated purpose is to keep such groups from being overlooked.
